title: The Bosphorus Brief — Sunday, 26 July 2026
overview: A quiet-ish Sunday for Türkiye itself — sport and summer travel dominate local headlines — while the wider region stays tense with the Iran-linked conflict spilling into the Red Sea and Gaza violence continuing. On the practical front: the lira held steady near 47.3/USD, the central bank left rates unchanged, and a top court decision on a decades-old case underscores how slowly some justice questions move here.
sections: <parameter name="heading">Money: Rates on hold, inflation forecasts creeping up
body: Türkiye's central bank held its policy rate at 37% for a fourth straight meeting, a move covered across pro-government and independent outlets alike with little disagreement on the facts. Separately, Deutsche Bank raised its Turkish inflation forecast to 30% for the year — a reminder for anyone budgeting in lira that price pressures remain a live issue. The exchange rate was steady this morning: USD/TRY 47.33, EUR/TRY 53.84, GBP/TRY 63.06. For residents paid in foreign currency, the rate itself is calm; the inflation trend is the number worth watching over rent and grocery costs.
